

## R02 Could you power your computer by typing?

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA

All visual facts below are OBSERVED unless labeled otherwise. Shot-specific composition and exact wording live only in [TIMELINE.csv](TIMELINE.csv). Asset variants live in [ASSET_MANIFEST.csv](ASSET_MANIFEST.csv).

| Category | Repeated rule | Exceptions / limits |
|---|---|---|
| Character DNA | Black circular/oval blank heads; stick limbs; no facial features, clothing detail or realistic skin. Held illustrated poses. | C03 headset and ponytail; C04 ponytail; C05 gray animal silhouette with eye/whiskers. Recurring graphic language does not prove character identity. |
| Environment DNA | Off-white empty field, large negative space; isolated desks/diagrams. | S01 board inset; S11 dark treatment; S12 gray grainy field; S13 outdoor canopy/ground. |
| Object DNA | Slightly irregular black contours; page-edge hatching, outlined devices, no photoreal surfaces. | Gray squirrel fill and solid black canopy; sparse scientific drawing texture. |
| Color palette | Dominant off-white about #F7F7F7, near-black ink, restrained muted red about #BD4146. | Values APPROXIMATE from decoded RGB, not original swatches. S11 dark field approximately #2D2D2D; S12 gray near #CECECE. |
| Lighting | Flat drawing with no changing cast shadows in most shots. | S11 six-frame darkening and six-frame recovery with soft stationary monitor light; S12 abrupt laptop light/rim appearance. |
| Camera / framing | 9:16, locked perspective within all 13 shots. No evidenced pan, dolly, zoom or shake. | Changes in drawing scale happen at hard cuts, not camera animation. Angled book/paper art is part of the drawing. |
| Composition | Clear isolated demonstration elements, approximate central/lower-middle scene placements, heavy use of top/bottom whitespace. | S04 intentionally crops page and keyboard; S11 words eventually fill field; S13 canopy fills upper-left. |
| Typography | Hand-lettered uppercase with irregular stroke/baseline; little decoration; exact scientific units retained. | Original typeface UNKNOWN. Scientific page body is squiggles; book body is dense real lettering with clipped parts. Never invent missing words. |
| Graphics | Small impact marks, curved explanatory leaders, red emphasis, word clouds, outlines and strike-throughs. | They communicate motion/typing but are often themselves completely still. |
| Illustration / 3D style | Flat 2D black-ink diagram/cartoon drawing. | No evidence of 3D rendering or particular software/model. |
| Depth | Overlap and local perspective in tables, books, keyboard and tree scene; no parallax. | No depth animation required. |
| Motion language | Hard overlay onset, localized still replacement, text/mask reveals. Most running/typing/pain action is implied by held drawings. | S07 black lettering and red strokes sometimes overlap in time; S11 brightness fades. |
| Transition language | 12 hard cuts; no crossfade between shots. Final frame holds to file end. | Fades are intra-shot lighting changes only. |
| Asset reuse | Stationary base plate plus additive annotations; reused typist/desk visual vocabulary; density variants for TAP/CLICK; registered pose replacements. | LIKELY layered assembly is an efficient explanation; the flattened source cannot prove the original layer organization. |

## Evidence and measurement conventions

Frame numbers are authoritative at 24 fps; millisecond times are rounded. Coordinates throughout are normalized top-left percentages unless expressly given in source pixels. A source-aligned 1080×1920 full-frame overlay at 100% scale is the simplest exact registration. In CapCut a center-origin position of (0,0) corresponds to full-frame center; do not mistake normalized source coordinates for inspector units.

A state can be a stable hold or a meaningful *reveal phase*. Continuous per-letter changes are grouped by word/line or strike, not inflated into hundreds of states. Motion endpoints may overlap the first complete-state frame. Instantaneous appearances occupy one frame in the motion map, followed by a hold in the timeline. Hard cuts are recorded in the timeline and are not counted again as object motion events.

No full-video dense image dump was needed. All 2,419 frames were decoded for change screening; sparse full-duration visual review plus adjacent change-pair review and targeted dense S07/text/fade sampling establish the sequence. Compression-only changes on held plates were excluded. Microvariation below this sampling/codec resolution is not treated as an intentional effect.


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# WAY 1 — CapCut reconstruction

## Project setup

- Canvas/aspect: 9:16 portrait. Resolution: 1080 × 1920. FPS: 24. Length: 2,419 frames (01:40.792 rounded).
- Background: E01 matched off-white; E02 for S12. Master audio: none in supplied source; leave A1/A2 empty.
- Global text system: T01. Original font UNKNOWN; source-derived/traced lettering gives the closest match. Editable native text is an approximation, matched by width, baseline and stroke weight.
- Global color: source-matched off-white, black and muted red. Global effects: NONE. Apply G14 only at its listed events.
- Import source as a temporary alignment/reference track, then hide it for export. Import the saved representative PNGs and the overlays specified in the manifest. Rebuilding still artwork and masks is the deliverable method; merely exporting the source video is not a reconstruction.

The following IDs are defined once in [ASSET_MANIFEST.csv](../02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv). Import the indicated formats and variants. Source-aligned full-frame PNGs are easiest to register; when cropping a local overlay, preserve its original source position. Background and a stationary illustration can share one plate. ## Frame-accurate assembly rules

1. Set still duration by frame count, not a rounded decimal drag. All times below are global. Use timeline row boundaries for exact clip lengths. Hard cuts get zero transition duration.
2. Register every full-frame source-aligned plate at 100% scale, center (0,0), zero rotation. When artwork is recreated at different bounds, match the evidence overlay at 50% opacity, then remove the alignment overlay. Positions/crop matches are APPROXIMATE until verified against the reference.
3. For a state replacement, split at the A-ID IN frame and start the new PNG/overlay at full opacity. Do not interpolate position or add stock entrance animation. The one-frame event interval records the change; keep its result until the next applicable event.
4. For reveals, animate a hard mask or crop over fixed artwork. A moving cover matching the background is an alternative when that version cannot keyframe a mask. For complex curves, a short sequence of traced progression PNGs gives tighter control inside CapCut.
5. For S07 use separate black text strips and red stroke layers. Preserve source baselines and line breaks; do not allow auto-wrapping or automatic caption layout. Per-frame x extents are available in the evidence CSV. Do not confuse a wipe through letters with a new hand-writing animation.
6. End with a held image on frame 2418. Export MP4/H.264, 1080×1920, 24 fps, no added audio. Check that the export contains 2,419 frames.

CapCut capability references: [official desktop keyframe help](https://www.capcut.com/help/keyframes-in-capcut-pc) supports position/scale/opacity controls; [official editing guide](https://www.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-capcut) covers masks. These establish available reconstruction controls, not the original production software. UI wording can differ by version.

### 04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md
# WAY 2 — Source image prompts

These are reusable source-image specifications, not claims that images have already been generated. Generate at 9:16/1080×1920 or a higher matching ratio, then register to the evidence. Text and diagram labels are not baked; source-derived overlays preserve exact wording. Reuse generated end frames only where the preceding state actually changes; never restart later actions from an unmodified base.

## Continuity masters

- CHARACTER: C02 uses blank oval head and simple stick limbs; retain scene-specific pose. C03 always keeps the same ponytail and headset shape. C04 remains a held running pose. No invented eyes/clothes or breathing.
- ENVIRONMENT: off-white flat field; only the recorded gray/dark/outdoor exceptions. No parallax or environment movement.
- OBJECT: retain desk/chair geometry, laptop angles, and measured book counts. Cables and socket panels are separate matched variants.
- STYLE: 2D irregular black ink, white interiors, limited gray fill and muted-red annotations. Original font/software/model/source library UNKNOWN.

Exact overlay wording, alignment and timing are in the canonical TIMELINE.csv and A-ID map. Image prompts below independently contain their own appearance specification. Tiny source text that cannot be read confidently is preserved as an evidence crop rather than invented.

### 04_image_to_video/ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md
# WAY 2 — Animation/event prompts

A-IDs are shared with MOTION_EVENTS.csv. Each prompt specifies only change. These are control prompts; exact text, one-frame replacements and short reveals should be executed deterministically during final assembly because generative interpolation would reduce fidelity. No prompt is provided for a static hold.

For every later event, SOURCE IMAGE means the named master **plus the current preceding composite state**. Preserve every already-added label, cloud and object. An instantaneous event needs a still replacement, not a generated movement clip. Its one-frame CLIP DURATION is the transition interval; the following held duration comes from TIMELINE.csv. For a reveal, the final changed frame is the fully visible target; OUT is exclusive.

For the two lighting events, a model supporting sufficiently short controlled clips may be tried with the supplied first/target state reference. If it drifts or cannot match timing, composite the fixed image with the measured opacity treatment in final assembly. This remains WAY 2. Never generate exact text or unnecessary character movement.

## R03 could_you_survive_nanosecond_sun

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA

## Observed global rules

- **Characters:** black, loose hand-drawn stick figures; circles for heads; no filled skin or clothing. Character scale changes only with composition changes.
- **Environments/objects:** white paper-like field with thin black line drawings. Cave scenes add ice overhangs, snow ground, and sparse dots. Scientific inserts use crisp diagrams, whiteboards, black field, or light gray sun-edge gradient.
- **Palette/lighting:** near-white ground, black lines, dark charcoal backgrounds, and sparse signal red annotations. A soft gray-white edge glow appears only in Sun/heat inserts.
- **Camera/composition:** locked full-frame 16:9 compositions. Cuts or panel replacement create most changes; no evidence of decorative camera drift, parallax, or depth of field.
- **Typography/graphics:** hand-lettered all-caps display labels and thin technical text. Exact words should be added as editor text where legibility matters. Red arrows, red “BAD” labels, and red crossed-out values are semantic emphasis.
- **Motion language:** drawings appear through short holds, hard cuts, panel swaps, simple translation, and incremental write-on/reveal states. Static drawings stay static after arrival.
- **Transition language:** hard cuts predominate. S03/S13 use a three-panel or doorway composition; S08 deliberately alternates black and white panels. S02/S14 are red identity/end cards.
- **Asset reuse:** C01 lecturer and E01 board recur; E02 cave and C02 explorer recur at opening and close. The Sun-edge gradient and C03 silhouette recur in comparison/exposure inserts.

## Scene-specific exceptions

- S02 and S14 replace monochrome illustration with solid red branded card.
- S08 alternates high-contrast black/gray and white technical panels; preserve cuts rather than blending them.
- S11 adds anatomical X-ray-like line art and a red warning placard to otherwise whiteboard staging.

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA

All points below OBSERVED unless marked.

## Global rules

- **Character DNA:** sparse black/white stick figures, round blank heads, single-line limbs; pose changes are cut replacements, not visible limb interpolation.
- **Environment DNA:** hand-drawn black outlines, flat white/grey/black fills. Maps, diagrams and board inserts use intentionally uneven ink-like contours.
- **Object DNA:** paper, screen frames, checklist and TV use thin black outlines. Red only marks dimensions, waterlines, locators and regional callouts.
- **Palette / lighting:** white ground, light grey field/water/land, deep black silhouettes; muted red accent. No visible lighting evolution.
- **Camera / framing:** locked portrait 9:16 canvas. Most explanatory scenes stack a 16:9 upper illustration above a lower presenter field; map dashboard uses black lower half. No observed camera pan, zoom, parallax or shake.
- **Typography:** hand-drawn all-caps, black on white or white on black. Use editor text overlays for exact readable wording; original font UNKNOWN.
- **Depth:** graphic layering only. Grey water behind black silhouettes; red callouts above maps.
- **Motion language:** predominantly still holds, hard cuts, instant text/callout/pose replacements. S05 alone visibly depicts fast downward radial descent. S02 water curtain is a state fill, not proven fluid simulation.
- **Transition language:** hard cut or instantaneous state replacement; no verified dissolve, wipe or camera-driven transition.
- **Asset reuse:** E01 display frame, E08 map dashboard, E09 island tableau, C03 presenter and T01 typography recur. Red annotation set changes per depth state rather than accumulating.

## Scene exceptions

- S05 has full-frame radial streak motion and is only scene requiring continuous animation.
- S14 substitutes detailed exposed-seafloor map E10 for simple map E08.
- S16 uses a standalone news-card composition; no lower presenter field.

## R05 earthquake-magnitude-shorts-wBLVmEZV2Oc

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# VISUAL DNA

Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in TIMELINE.csv / ASSET_MANIFEST.csv — not repeated here.

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
- Flat solid white/off-white canvas for the entire video (OBSERVED). No background photography, no gradients, no depth layers.
- No camera moves, no parallax, no depth-of-field anywhere (OBSERVED — zero scene cuts detected, all "cuts" are 2D layer swaps on the same flat canvas).

## CHARACTER DNA
- One recurring minimalist stick-figure design (circle head, straight-line limbs, no facial detail beyond dot eyes) reused across 4 poses/props (interview duo, NASA-badge figure, distressed figure, headset figure). See C01.

## OBJECT / ILLUSTRATION DNA
- Uniform hand-drawn / sketch line-art style for every illustration (seismograph, newspaper, globe, fault-block slabs, debris) — black ink linework, thin uniform stroke weight, minimal or flat grey shading, no gradients or 3D rendering (OBSERVED).
- Central recurring visual metaphor: a grey globe/Earth icon that accumulates visible "damage" states as the fictional magnitude escalates (clean → epicenter marks → cracked → spiky border → exploded debris). This is the emotional/visual throughline of the whole piece (OBSERVED progression, LIKELY intentional escalation device).
- Red ink is reserved exclusively for "alert/annotation" marks: strike-throughs, circles, epicenter ripples, the climbing scribble — never used for the base illustrations (OBSERVED, consistent rule across the whole video).

## COLOR PALETTE
- Background: white/off-white (#FFFFFF-ish).
- Line art: black.
- Fills: flat light-to-mid grey (globe, slabs).
- Accent: red (annotations, alerts, epicenters, "danger" scribbles) — the only saturated color used anywhere in the video (OBSERVED).

## TYPOGRAPHY (T01/T02)
- T01 (titles): bold, all-caps, hand-drawn/marker-style sans-serif, large, centered top of canvas.
- T02 (captions/annotations): same type family, much smaller, regular weight, used for facts, dates, measurements, and punchlines.
- No other type styles appear anywhere in the video (OBSERVED).

## GRAPHICS / UI LANGUAGE
- E02 (the vertical ruler/number-line) is the single persistent HUD element from F01.5 onward — it never fully disappears once introduced, acting as a constant visual reminder of "where we are on the scale" (OBSERVED).
- G01 ("LIVE" broadcast box) is a reusable template appearing 3 times with different internal content — the video's go-to device for a punchline/reaction beat (OBSERVED reuse pattern).

## COMPOSITION
- Every state is centered, single-column, vertically stacked (title → illustration → optional caption/box), consistent with 9:16 short-form framing (OBSERVED).

## MOTION LANGUAGE
- No camera motion anywhere. All motion is 2D layer animation: fade-ins, one draw-on (strike-through, circle), one continuous scale-up (the ruler, once), and hard cuts between major "screens" (OBSERVED — see MOTION_EVENTS.csv).
- Hard cuts are used specifically at every full-topic change (new magnitude number); fades/draw-ons are used for additions *within* a topic. This is a consistent authorial rule (LIKELY intentional pacing device).

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
- Two transition types only: (1) instant hard cut (STATE_REPLACEMENT, used ~11 times at major beats) and (2) opacity fade-in (used for additive annotations within a state). No wipes, no slides, no 3D transitions anywhere (OBSERVED).

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
- High reuse of structural templates (G01 LIVE box x3, C01 stick figure x4 poses, E02 ruler throughout, E03 globe across 4 damage states) vs. single-use "punchline" illustrations (E01 seismograph, O01 newspaper, O02 phone, O03 fault-blocks) that appear exactly once each. This 80/20 pattern (few reusable structural assets + many disposable gag assets) is the core efficiency pattern of the production (OBSERVED).

## FIDELITY LIMITATION
- Sub-0.5-second easing curves (exact fade durations, exact scale-up curve of the ruler, exact rotation speed of the globe) cannot be measured precisely from 2fps sampling; all such values are marked APPROXIMATE or LIKELY in MOTION_EVENTS.csv rather than fabricated as exact numbers.


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# CAPCUT REBUILD — earthquake-magnitude-shorts-wBLVmEZV2Oc

Reference: TIMELINE.csv (timing/content per state), ASSET_MANIFEST.csv (every asset ID), MOTION_EVENTS.csv (every A-ID). This file only adds CapCut-specific build steps — it does not repeat descriptions already in those files.

## PROJECT SETUP
- CANVAS / ASPECT RATIO: 9:16
- RESOLUTION: 1080x1920
- FPS: 24
- TOTAL DURATION: 65.96s (round timeline to 66s)
- BACKGROUND: solid white (#FFFFFF), set as canvas color for the whole project (no background clip needed)
- MASTER AUDIO: AU01 narration (write/record new lines per state, see AUDIO_MAP.md) + optional AU02 music bed, low volume, ducked under narration
- GLOBAL FONT/TEXT SYSTEM: one bold hand-drawn/marker-style caps font for T01 (titles), same family at smaller regular weight for T02 (captions) — pick one CapCut font (e.g. "Permanent Marker" or similar bundled font) and reuse for both via size/weight variation only
- GLOBAL COLOR RULE: black line art + grey flat fills on white canvas; red reserved only for annotation/alert marks (strike-throughs, circles, epicenter rings, scribbles) — never used elsewhere
- GLOBAL EFFECTS: none (no filters, no LUTs, no vignette observed)

## MEDIA TO IMPORT
Reference ASSET_MANIFEST.csv for full descriptions. Import as transparent PNGs unless noted:
T01, T02 (built as CapCut text layers, not images), E01, O01, O02, G01 (one frame, reused 3x), C01 (4 pose variants), E02 (ruler — build as CapCut shapes+text, not an image, so it can be keyframed), E03 (4 damage-state PNGs, or 1 base + 3 additive overlay PNGs), O05, O03, O04 (2 density variants), AU01, AU02.

## SHOT BUILD
Single shot (S01) end-to-end — this project is one continuous canvas with layers cutting in/out, not multiple video clips. Build it as one long timeline with clip/image layers trimmed to each state's IN/OUT.

### F01.0-F01.2 — Intro gag (0.00-4.60s)
TRACK STACK: V2 T01 title text | V1 E01 seismograph
BUILD:
1. Place T01 text "RICHTER SCALE" 0.00-1.60s.
2. At 1.60s, duplicate the text clip; apply CapCut's "Strikethrough"-style effect or overlay a thin red rectangle shape animated left-to-right (position keyframe, 1.60s→2.10s) across the text to fake a strike-through.
3. Add second T01 text "\"MOMENT MAGNITUDE\" SCALE" below, opacity keyframe 0%→100% from 1.80s-2.30s.
4. Place E01 clip 0.00-4.60s. If E01 is a static PNG, add a short looping "shake" via position keyframes (small random X/Y jitter, amplitude ~5px) starting 1.60s; if E01 is a pre-animated video clip with the ink-scribble baked in, just trim it to 2.60-4.60s for that portion.
KEYFRAMES: 00:01.600 — red strike shape opacity 0→100 / 00:02.100 — strike hold / 00:01.800 — T01 line2 opacity 0→100 (APPROXIMATE timings)
TOOLS: keyframes, opacity, shape overlay, position (jitter)
TRANSITION: none in (video start) / hard CUT out at 4.60s
AUDIO SYNC: narration line 1 starts 0.00s; line 2 ("well actually, it's the moment magnitude scale") starts ~1.60s
END STATE: F01.2
FIDELITY LIMITATION: CapCut has no native "hand-drawn scribble" brush; fastest approximation is a pre-rendered PNG/video asset for E01 with the scribble baked in, animated only via position keyframes in CapCut.

### F01.3-F01.4 — Newspaper / phone / LIVE box gag (5.00-8.00s)

1. Cut all V1/V2 (F01.0-2 layers) at 4.60s; new layers in at 5.00s (0.4s hard black-frame gap or straight cut — OBSERVED as instant cut, treat as a straight cut with no transition).
2. Place O01 top third, O02 bottom-left third, G01+C01+T02 bottom-right third, all in 5.00-8.00s.

KEYFRAMES: 00:06.000 — circle shape opacity 0→100, scale 0→100 (APPROXIMATE)
TOOLS: cutout, position, opacity, shape, keyframes
TRANSITION IN: CUT / TRANSITION OUT: CUT (8.50s)

END STATE: F01.4

### F01.5-F01.9 — The real scale + the fact (8.50-18.10s)
TRACK STACK: V2 T01/T02 text | V1 E02 ruler (built from shapes: one vertical line + repeated small tick-mark lines + number text layers)
BUILD:
1. Build E02 as a CapCut compound: 1 vertical line shape + a stack of short horizontal tick shapes + text numbers, grouped.
2. 8.50-9.00s: short ruler (scale Y ~30%).
3. 9.00-12.50s: keyframe the group's Y-scale from ~30%→70%, and swap in numbered tick text at 12.50s (or reveal a pre-built "numbered" version via opacity crossfade).
4. 13.00-13.60s: continue Y-scale keyframe 70%→100%; simultaneously bring in T02 caption text block (opacity 0→100), replacing an earlier shorter placeholder caption if you built one, or simply have the caption appear once at 13.60s if you skip the intermediate wording change (LOW fidelity cost, OBSERVED difference is minor).
5. 14.60-15.60s: T01 + T02 opacity 100→0.
6. 16.00-17.50s: overlay a red scribble PNG/shape group over the ruler's mid-section, with a fast opacity flicker or small looped jitter to fake vibration, then opacity 100→0 at 17.50-18.10s.
KEYFRAMES: 00:09.000 ruler scaleY 30%→70% (out 12.500) / 00:13.000 ruler scaleY 70%→100% (out 13.600) / 00:14.600 T01+T02 opacity 100→0 (out 15.600) / 00:16.000 scribble opacity 0→100 (out 16.400), jitter loop 16.400-17.400, opacity 100→0 (out 17.500) — all APPROXIMATE
TOOLS: shape, text, keyframes, opacity, scale
TRANSITION: fades throughout, no hard cuts inside this block
AUDIO SYNC: caption fact line reads during 13.60-15.60s hold
END STATE: F01.9
FIDELITY LIMITATION: exact ruler growth easing curve is unmeasurable at 0.5s sampling — use CapCut's default "ease-out" keyframe curve as a reasonable approximation.

### F01.10-F01.22 — Magnitude escalation ladder (18.50-65.96s)
TRACK STACK (constant from here on): V4 G01+C01+T02 (LIVE boxes, when present) | V3 illustration layer (E03 globe / O03 slabs / O04 debris, one at a time) | V2 T01/T02 text | V1 E02 ruler (persistent, never removed)
BUILD PATTERN (repeats per magnitude step — see TIMELINE.csv for each state's exact IN/OUT and content):

5. For A24 (ruler's subtle upward reframe near the end): optionally add a slow position keyframe on E02 (Y position drifting up a few px from 48.50s to the end) — this is a LOW-fidelity-risk optional touch, skip if not visible enough to matter.
KEYFRAMES: see MOTION_EVENTS.csv IN/OUT columns per A-ID — apply the same opacity-fade or straight-cut pattern noted above for each
TOOLS: cutout, opacity, keyframes, crossfade, position (optional for A24)
TRANSITION: hard CUTs between magnitude steps, opacity fades for additions within a step
AUDIO SYNC: each "MAGNITUDE N" cut should land on a narration beat/number callout; LIVE-box gags get a deadpan-delivery narration line
END STATE: F01.22 (video end)

## R06 how_long_could_you_drive_towards_the_sunset

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA — how_long_could_you_drive_towards_the_sunset

Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`/`ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`; this file states only repeated rules and their exceptions.

## CHARACTER DNA
- Repeated rule: humans are rendered as minimal stick figures — a plain circle head with no facial features and thin line limbs (C01), used identically as a reader, desk-worker, and pedestrian.
- Exceptions or limits: the camera-crew pair (C02) is a distinct, more detailed silhouette design (visible hair, tripod camera prop) reserved only for the two photographic-style sunset shots (S03, S14); it never appears in the flat-diagram shots.

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
- Repeated rule: two visually distinct backdrop families recur — (1) a plain white canvas for schematic/diagram shots, and (2) painterly gradient-sky backdrops for "real-world" location shots (E02 polar dusk, E07 ocean sunset).
- Exceptions or limits: E01 (chalkboard) and E05 (office desk) and E06 (church) are unique single-shot environments that don't recur or blend with the two main families.

## OBJECT DNA
- Repeated rule: the sun/shadow relationship is always drawn as a small flat yellow circle (G01) paired with a small flat grey circle (G02), regardless of which larger diagram it appears in (horizon chains, mountain rolls, recap insets, map legends).
- Exceptions or limits: in the two full-scale "real" location shots (S07, S08) and the two photographic sunset shots (S03, S14), the sun is instead rendered as a larger illustrated/painterly disc, not the small flat schematic circle.

## COLOR PALETTE
- Repeated rule: diagram shots use a restricted grey/black/white/yellow palette (white canvas, black line art, yellow sun accents, grey shadow accents), with red reserved exclusively for rejection marks (X), directional arrows, and callout labels.
- Exceptions or limits: the two photographic sunset shots (S03, S14) and the two polar establishing shots (S07, S08) use a full painterly gradient palette (deep blue/purple night sky through red-orange-yellow sunset colors) that departs from the flat diagram palette.

## LIGHTING
- Repeated rule: diagram shots are flat and shadeless (no rendered light source other than labeled sun/shadow icons).
- Exceptions or limits: the photographic/painterly shots (S03, S07, S08, S14) simulate directional light via gradient skies and a glowing sun disc with a water/ice reflection.

## CAMERA / FRAMING
- Repeated rule: every shot in this video uses a static, locked camera — OBSERVED across all 14 shots; no pans, zooms, or tracking moves were detected anywhere in the source.
- Exceptions or limits: none observed. (The apparent "movement" in several shots — cars, sun circles, terminator arrows — is graphic-element motion within a fixed frame, not camera motion.)

## COMPOSITION
- Repeated rule: diagram shots are built around a single dominant horizontal reference line (a horizon line, a globe terminator, or a map's day/night band) with graphic elements arranged along or around it.
- Exceptions or limits: the chalkboard shot (S01) and photographic shots (S03/S14) are composed as full-bleed single-subject frames rather than around a horizontal reference line.

## TYPOGRAPHY
- Repeated rule: all on-screen text is a single consistent white, hand-lettered/rounded sans-serif caption style, used for location labels, data callouts, and dialogue.
- Exceptions or limits: none observed — caption styling is uniform across all shots that carry text (S03, S05-S14).

## GRAPHICS
- Repeated rule: rejection/confirmation is always communicated with a red hand-drawn X (wrong) or green check mark (right), never with color grading, sound stingers alone, or a spoken-only "no."
- Exceptions or limits: none observed.

## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
- Repeated rule: flat 2D vector/line-art illustration dominates (chalkboard, all circle/horizon diagrams, map shots, desk/church shots).
- Exceptions or limits: S06 uses a pseudo-3D wireframe/graticule globe render (grid lines suggesting a sphere in perspective) — the only shot with any implied 3D depth; S03/S07/S08/S14 use painterly/gradient rendering rather than flat vector fills.

## DEPTH
- Repeated rule: diagram shots are single-plane (foreground graphics directly on a flat background, no midground layer).
- Exceptions or limits: the photographic sunset and polar-location shots (S03, S07, S08, S14) use a simple foreground/background depth split (silhouette figures or vehicles in front of a gradient sky/horizon).

## MOTION LANGUAGE
- Repeated rule: nearly all motion in this video is graphic-element reveal/build (objects, arrows, and captions being progressively drawn onto an otherwise static frame) rather than continuous physical animation; OBSERVED across S02, S04-S06, S08-S14.
- Exceptions or limits: S01's globe spin, S04's mountain-roll gag, and S10/S12's car-advancing-along-a-path are the only cases of an element continuously translating/rotating rather than simply appearing.

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
- Repeated rule: shot changes are hard cuts (OBSERVED via the `ffmpeg` scene-change filter for 11 of the 13 inter-shot boundaries).
- Exceptions or limits: two boundaries (S07→S08 and S13→S14) were not flagged by the automated scene-change detector despite a clear visual content change; these are labeled LIKELY DISSOLVE / LIKELY CUT respectively in `TIMELINE.csv` based on direct frame comparison rather than the detector.

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
- Repeated rule: the small schematic sun/shadow circle pair (G01/G02) and the horizon-line motif (G03) are the throughline connecting nearly every diagram shot (S02, S04, S09, S10, S12, S13); the video's two "bookend" photographic sunset shots (S03, S14) reuse the exact same background plate (E07) and character pair (C02).
- Exceptions or limits: the North Pole (S07) and Longyearbyen (S08) establishing shots share a sky-gradient language (E02) but do NOT share foreground assets — each has its own unique vehicle and background silhouette.

## Evidence and measurement conventions
- All timing is expressed in frames at the source's true constant frame rate: 24fps, 3117 total frames, 129.875s video duration.
- Shot/state boundaries were established primarily from 130 source-resolution 1fps frame extractions, cross-checked against `ffmpeg` scene-change detection at thresholds 0.25 and 0.10. Two shot boundaries were not confirmed by the automated detector (see Transition Language above) and are marked LIKELY rather than OBSERVED for their exact frame-level cut point; all other boundaries are OBSERVED at 1-second precision.
- Long/continuous motions (A09 mountain roll, A24 car-and-legend advance) were confirmed smooth and single-direction via 1s interval sampling, not exhaustive native-frame verification; their internal easing/pacing is LIKELY steady rather than confirmed exact.

## Reuse decisions
- S14 does not get its own source image: it reuses IMG03's exact plate and character silhouettes verbatim as a deliberate visual bookend to S03, differing only in caption overlay content (T04 dialogue instead of T01) and the added swirl motion graphic (A30) — regenerating a near-identical image would duplicate an asset the reference itself reuses.
- Every other shot (S01, S02, S04-S13) requires its own unique image because each has a substantially different background, composition, or environment from every other shot in this video — unlike more repetitive explainer videos, this one rarely revisits the same setting twice, so image reuse here is limited to the one genuine callback (S03/S14).
- IMG07 and IMG08 intentionally share the same sky-gradient illustration language (described identically in both prompts) to preserve visual continuity between the two "real-world location" shots, even though they are generated as two separate images due to their different foreground content (ice+seals+tractor vs. mountain-ridge+car).

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA

## Global observed rules

- **Character DNA — OBSERVED:** thin, black, hand-drawn stick figures; occasional red outline/speckled disintegration state. One presenter figure sometimes carries a paper or speaks via curved callout line.
- **Environment DNA — OBSERVED:** sparse diagrammatic spaces: white paper-like fields, charcoal night fields, black silhouette ground, grey midtones. Buildings, machinery and props are ink outlines with deliberately uneven strokes.
- **Object DNA — OBSERVED:** simple, high-contrast technical icons; many have no shading beyond grey fill. Nuclear/cesium items add cyan emission; failures use red detail.
- **Palette — OBSERVED:** near-white, black, cool greys; red is alert/disappearance/accent; cyan is radioactive/energy glow; end card is flat red with black and white.
- **Lighting — OBSERVED:** localized soft white pools for lamps and night scenes. Industrial daytime frames are flat white. Cyan objects have a soft outer glow. No photorealistic lighting.
- **Camera/framing — OBSERVED:** locked orthographic-like 2D view. No evidence of camera pan, dolly, perspective parallax, or lens behavior. Reframing occurs by hard cut or a graphic wipe/slide.
- **Composition — OBSERVED:** left-to-right explanatory staging; large negative space around diagrams; panels divide comparisons. Text is placed in clear unused space, usually top or center.
- **Typography — OBSERVED:** hand-lettered, black, mostly all caps. Exact font unknown. Exact readable labels should be editor text, not image-generated text.
- **Graphics — OBSERVED:** black callout lines, speech lines, warning symbols, panel borders, simple graphs and white/grey cards.
- **Depth/style — OBSERVED:** flat 2D line illustration with silhouette layers; no observable 3D material or depth-of-field.
- **Motion language — OBSERVED:** sparse sequential substitutions: lights extinguish, people convert to red particles, icons/cards appear, panels reveal, decay texture grows, rain overlays, and a final object splits. Static holds dominate.
- **Transition language — OBSERVED:** hard cuts dominate. Some darken/fade-to-black, lateral reveal/slide, and simple element pop-ins occur. No evidence of decorative motion between every state.
- **Reuse — LIKELY:** recurring visual vocabulary (same stick figures, pylon, wind turbine, lamp glow, warning signs, handwritten text treatment) is reused, but source files are UNKNOWN.

## Scene exceptions

- S02 and S26 are branded red cards, not part of normal monochrome explanatory field.
- S19 uses concentric rings behind a large wristwatch; S21–S25 add cyan energy/radiation glow.
- S16 uses a richer night roadside environment and rain overlay; camera stays locked.

## Reconstruction constraints

Use 24 fps, 16:9, locked framing, hand-drawn black outlines and off-white/grey fields. Red and cyan only where timeline assigns them. No global film grain, camera shake, parallax, bounce, or ambient particles. Any live texture in rain/disintegration must be limited to its assigned A-ID.

## R08 if_toaster_in_freezer

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA

## Observed global rules

- **Character DNA:** black-outline stick figures; circular heads; minimal facial detail. Some figures add black hair, beard, glasses, or a wrapped head.
- **Environment DNA:** white paper-like field, sparse hand-drawn linework, thin black borders; scenes replace rather than share a literal continuous room.
- **Object DNA:** simplified black-outline appliances and props. Toaster red/orange glow is repeated visual shorthand for heat.
- **Palette / lighting:** near-white background, black line art, restrained red accent. Outdoor scene uses a grey night wash; title/end card use flat red.
- **Camera / composition:** locked, orthographic-looking wide compositions. Changes are primarily hard cuts or whole-frame replacements; no evidenced decorative camera drift.
- **Typography / graphics:** irregular hand-drawn uppercase and handwritten labels; scientific annotations use thin black type with red arrows/heat lines.
- **Depth:** flat 2D layers with rare soft red glow around hot appliances.
- **Motion language:** draw-on/reveal, state replacement, pop-in, opacity fade, and very short object/character pose swaps. Static holds dominate.
- **Transition language:** hard cuts, one early full-frame push/replacement, one fade-to-dark in outdoor scene, and red bumper/end-card cuts.
- **Asset reuse:** toaster, freezer/refrigerator motif, black-line character language, and red heat treatment recur across otherwise new plates.

## Scene exceptions

- S03 and S12 use branded red graphic cards rather than white line-art scenes.
- S10 is grey night exterior; its red toaster remains chromatic focal point.
- S08 is technical cutaway/diagram rather than character narrative.

## Evidence limits

Exact font, production software, original drawing source, music identity, and easing curves are UNKNOWN.


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# CapCut rebuild

## Project setup

- Canvas: 16:9 landscape, 1920 x 1080, 24 fps; total 02:42.261.
- Background: white for line-art shots; use E03/E12 red full-frame plates where called.
- Master audio: AU01 extracted from source MP4; lock before visual editing.
- Text: T01 closest hand-drawn uppercase/handwriting match. Use native text for exact readable words; never bake generator text.
- Color: black line art on near-white; red only for heat, diagrams, title/end-card fields.
- Global effects: none. Use local red glow only in F04.5, F07.2, F08.7, F09.2, F10.4–F10.7; grey opacity wash only F02.5 and F10.1 onward.

## Media to import

`C01–C04, E01–E12, O01–O05, G01–G03, T01, AU01` from `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`. Build each E plate clean; use transparent overlays for objects/graphics that change. For each listed state replacement, an exported state plate is valid and closer than invented interpolation.

## Fidelity limits

- Frame times are sampled to 0.25 s; use AU01 waveform and frame matching to refine in/out to individual 24 fps frames.
- Source font, exact effects, and original assets are UNKNOWN. State plates are more faithful than adding non-evidenced motion.

## R09 weird_and_worrying_questions

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA — weird_and_worrying_questions

Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file states the repeated rule once and notes exceptions.

## CHARACTER DNA
Repeated rule: a single plain bald stick figure (C01) — round head, minimal limbs, no facial features beyond an implied gaze — seated at a desk for the entire video; this is the sole recurring "on-camera" character.
Exceptions: C02 (hat + trenchcoat + magnifying glass) appears once, single-use, for the "mirrors" aside (F01.8) and never recurs. A second, distinct illustrated stick figure (G06, the "imagined self" inside the thought bubble) and a crying figure (G11) are graphic elements, not the on-camera character C01.

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
Repeated rule: flat plain white background (E01) for the entire runtime; no set dressing beyond the desk.
Exceptions: none observed.

## OBJECT DNA
Repeated rule: the desk + monitor + keyboard (O01) is a fixed, static prop present and unmoving in every state.
Exceptions: a physical coffee mug (O02) is held by C01 only in the opening joke (F01.0–F01.5) and is thrown off-panel during F01.6; it never reappears.

## COLOR PALETTE
Repeated rule: pure black line-art on white, matching a hand-drawn/xkcd-style aesthetic; the only non-monochrome element is the red mercury column inside the thermometer (G03).
Exceptions: none.

## LIGHTING
Repeated rule: flat, shadowless line-art; no lighting model present.

## CAMERA / FRAMING
Repeated rule: **one fixed, locked camera position for the entire video** — no cuts, pans, zooms, or reframing were observed anywhere. This is the video's defining structural trait and is why the whole runtime is modeled as a single shot (S01). All apparent "cuts" from scene-cut detection are large content swaps within this one static frame (thought-bubble graphics appearing/clearing, a second character entering/exiting), not camera changes.
Exceptions: none.

## COMPOSITION
Repeated rule: C01 + desk occupy the lower-right area of frame; a gray question card (T01), when present, sits top-left; the thought bubble (G01), when present, occupies the upper-center/upper-left area above C01.
Exceptions: the two "plaque" states (F01.21–F01.22) replace the Q-card + bubble layout with a single full-frame graphic (G10); the closing caption states (F01.25–F01.26) show no bubble or Q-card at all, only a short caption line above C01.

## TYPOGRAPHY
Repeated rule: two distinct text systems are used consistently — T01 (a gray rounded-rectangle "Q" card with sentence-case question body text and a "— Name" attribution line, used for all five named questions) and T02 (bold, all-caps, hand-drawn-style caption text with occasional underline emphasis, used for asides/punchlines/reactions that are not attributed questions).
Exceptions: none.

## GRAPHICS
Repeated rule: every gag illustration (teeth, thermometer, mirror/star array, volcano, reactor, plaque, crying figure) is a bespoke single-use graphic drawn inside or replacing the thought bubble; none are reused across different jokes.
Exceptions: the thought-bubble container outline itself (G01) is the one recurring graphic, reused as a frame for five of the six gags.

## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
Repeated rule: loose hand-drawn black-ink vector/sketch style, consistent with the same illustration language used elsewhere in this project (matches `what_if_the_moon_were_made_of_protons` and `how_long_could_you_drive_towards_the_sunset`).

## DEPTH
Repeated rule: flat 2D compositing throughout; no foreground/midground/background layering beyond the character+desk vs. bubble-content plane.

## MOTION LANGUAGE
Repeated rule: nearly every state transition is a **content swap** (a graphic or caption appears, fully formed, or clears to blank) rather than a continuous physical animation; genuine continuous motion is limited to two cases — the thermometer's mercury drop (A03) and the crying figure's growing puddle (A23). No camera movement, parallax, particles, or decorative motion of any kind was observed anywhere.
Exceptions: the mug-throw (A06) is the one instance of an object undergoing a translating motion (off-panel).

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
Repeated rule: all transitions between visual states are hard content cuts/fades within the single locked frame (bubble/Q-card content appears or clears); there are no wipes, dissolves, or camera-driven transitions.

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
Repeated rule: this video has the lowest reuse profile of any video in this project — of 19 total assets, only C01, E01, O01, G01, T01, T02 and AU01 (7 of 19) recur across multiple states; the remaining 12 assets (C02, O02, G02–G11 minus G01) are single-use, one per gag, reflecting the video's fast joke-per-question structure (six independent question/answer gags in ~47 seconds).


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# WAY 1 — CapCut Reconstruction — weird_and_worrying_questions

This entire video is **one locked-camera shot (S01)**; there are no camera cuts to rebuild. All 27 visual states are built as layer/keyframe changes on a single canvas. Reference `../02_analysis/TIMELINE.csv` (SHOT_ID/STATE_ID) and `../02_analysis/MOTION_EVENTS.csv` (MOTION_ID) instead of repeating descriptions here.

## CapCut project setup
- CANVAS / ASPECT RATIO: 9:16
- RESOLUTION: 1080x1920
- FPS: 24
- TOTAL DURATION: 00:47.458 (1139 frames)
- BACKGROUND: solid white (E01), full duration
- MASTER AUDIO: AU01, single continuous track from 00:00.000
- GLOBAL FONT/TEXT SYSTEM: two text styles reused throughout — T01 (Q-card: gray rounded-rectangle shape, sentence-case body text, smaller bold "— Name" line) and T02 (bold all-caps hand-drawn-style font, selective underline for emphasis)
- GLOBAL COLOR RULE: black line art on white; red fill reserved for the thermometer mercury (G03) only
- GLOBAL EFFECTS: none (no filters, LUTs, or transitions beyond hard cuts/fades on individual layers)

KEYFRAMES: only listed where an element's position/scale/opacity actually changes (A03 mercury, A06 mug throw, A23 puddle growth); all other transitions are hard cuts/fades between static PNG variants, per the Absolute Fidelity Rule (no invented easing beyond a simple 0.2–0.3s opacity fade where noted).

TOOLS: opacity, position keyframes, scale keyframes, crop/mask (for G03 mercury), cutout/overlay layering, text (native CapCut for T01/T02).

TEXT: exact wording for every T01/T02 instance is given verbatim in `../02_analysis/TIMELINE.csv`'s `LITERAL_FRAME_DESCRIPTION` and `SCRIPT_OR_AUDIO_CUE` columns; reproduce as native CapCut text layers rather than baking into images (see `../04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md` TEXT BAKED policy).

TRANSITION: hard cuts throughout; the only soft fades observed are the ~0.2–0.3s opacity fade-ins noted above for newly appearing bubble graphics (A01, A02, A05, A08, A10, A12, A18).

AUDIO SYNC: AU01 plays continuously from 00:00.000; the four measured near-silence gaps (see `../05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md`) fall at ≈34.5s (during the Chernobyl/plaque transition, A19–A20) and ≈45.5–47.3s (during the closing Karl caption beats, A24–A25) — APPROXIMATE sync only, no transcript available.

END STATE: F01.26 (video ends).

FIDELITY LIMITATION: because this is a single continuous canvas rather than discrete camera shots, CapCut reconstruction requires careful layer-visibility sequencing (toggling V4/V5 content per segment) rather than simple shot-to-shot cutting; get the V1–V2 layers (E01/O01/C01) right once and never re-cut them for the whole 47.458s.

## R10 what-if-earth-grew-1cm-every-second

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA

## Observed global rules

- Hand-drawn, thin black line illustration on near-white field; gray pencil-like hatching fills Earth, objects, and shadows.
- Stick-figure presenter/people recur. Geometry is flat, centered or side-by-side, with broad empty space.
- Time labels occupy a black strip at top on many explanatory scenes: `T = ...` in small white uppercase text.
- Important numerical change uses red handwritten-style text, red underline, or red arrow. Most explanatory text is black uppercase hand lettering.
- Camera is normally locked, full-frame 16:9. Major changes are hard cuts; whiteboard composition is reused. No observed decorative parallax, bloom, particles, or continuous camera drift.
- Motion language is sparse: draw-on/reveal, object/graphic replacement, simple translation, scale change, sequential collapse, and occasional diagram line growth. Static holds are common.

## Exceptions

- S02 and S39 use flat red branded title/end cards with black illustration and white text.
- S37–S38 use a black space field, grayscale Earth/Moon, thin orbit lines, and white satellite drawings.
- S03 briefly uses a dark cave/opening inside a whiteboard drawing.

## Reconstruction consequence

Keep backgrounds locked. Build exact text as editor overlays, not generated-image text. Treat source-specific artwork, fonts, music, editor, model, lens, and stock source as UNKNOWN.


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# CapCut rebuild

## Project setup

- Canvas: 16:9, 1920 × 1080; 24 fps; total 05:15.675.
- Background: near-white (`#F7F7F5` approximate) unless listed black (S37–S38) or red (S02/S39). Global effects: none observed.
- Audio: put `AU01` / `../05_audio/source_audio.wav` on A1 at 00:00.000; lock it. Narration/music/SFX split is UNKNOWN.
- Text system: manual text/shape layers only. Small uppercase time strip is white on black; numerical emphasis/red arrows use muted red. Exact unrecovered tiny text stays source-frame transcription work, not invented.
- Import media: all listed IDs from `../02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`. Build vector diagrams as SVG/shape/text layers; use transparent PNG layers for characters, objects, and silhouettes.

# Animation prompts

## A01 — S01 — IMG01 — F01.0 to F01.1 — 4.667 s

## R11 what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA — what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam

Global, repeated production patterns. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file is not repeated there.

| Dimension | Repeated rule | Exceptions / limits |
|---|---|---|
| CHARACTER DNA | One recurring minimal stick-figure (circle head, thin line limbs, holding a paper) in S01 only; a labeled human silhouette (line-art) in S02 only. No character reappears across shots. | No characters appear after S02; the rest of the video is diagrams/objects only. |
| ENVIRONMENT DNA | Three backdrop families reused across most shots: (1) plain black starfield (E02, most of the runtime), (2) grey chalkboard (E01, S01 only), (3) side-view cross-section of sky+planetary-arc+continent (E03, S04 and S09). | Dusk graveyard (E04) is unique to S06 and does not recur. |
| OBJECT DNA | A single Earth/Moon iconography family recurs at three levels of realism: shaded/detailed (G09), plain half-lit sphere (G11), and simplified black outline (G13); the Moon is always a small plain grey circle (G14) until it is damaged (G17, red/cracked). | The chalkboard's tiny Earth icon (G02) is a fourth, simpler style used only in S01/S03; it is not the same asset as G09/G11/G13. |
| COLOR PALETTE | Two-mode palette: neutral grey/black/white for exposition (S01-S03, S07, S10-S12), with a single accent — glowing white for the light source/beam — throughout. Red/pink is reserved exclusively for damage, danger, or destruction (plasma dome, cracks, "NOT SAFE!", the ring, the comet, the shattered Moon). | S06's graveyard is the only shot with a distinct purple-to-pink dusk sky; S01 is the only shot on an off-white/grey chalkboard rather than black. |
| LIGHTING | Flat, shadeless illustration lighting throughout; the only "light" rendered as light is the glow/beam graphic itself (G03/G05), used consistently as a bright white radial or linear glow with soft falloff. | None observed. |
| CAMERA / FRAMING | 9:16 vertical lock. Camera is static (no zoom/dolly/rotation) in 14 of 15 shots. | S06 (graveyard) is the only shot with OBSERVED camera motion: a lateral pan across a row of gravestones. Do not add camera motion to any other shot. |
| COMPOSITION | Recurring "vertical beam down the center third" composition anchors S01, S04, S05, S07, S08, S09, S11, S12, S13 — the beam or its target sits on/near the vertical centerline with labels/arrows branching to the sides. | S02, S03, S06, S10, S14, S15 break from this (S02/S03 have no discrete target object yet; S06/S14/S15 have no beam in frame). |
| TYPOGRAPHY | Two caption styles: a thin hand-drawn-style sans caption for callouts/labels/stats (T01, T03, T04, T05, T07), and a bolder carved/serif-ish style reserved for the tombstone text (T06). | Exact typeface is UNKNOWN/unverifiable; recreate by visual matching only, per fidelity rules. |
| GRAPHICS | Arrow-and-label callout pairs (thin line arrow + short caption) are the dominant graphic device, appearing in S01, S04, S05, S07, S11. | The subatomic-particle glyphs (G04) and the twin ring effects (G12 twilight-ring vs. G15 shockwave-ring) are one-off/twice-only devices — do not conflate the two rings, they differ in scale, speed, and narrative meaning. |
| ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE | Flat 2D vector-style illustration throughout; no 3D rendering, no photographic elements, no particle-simulation-grade detail (sparks/debris are simple flecks and jagged line strokes, not simulated). | None observed. |
| DEPTH | Consistently shallow/flat: foreground subject + plain background, no midground layer, in every shot. | None observed. |
| MOTION LANGUAGE | Motion is almost entirely "reveal" (fade-in of text/graphics) or "radial growth" (dome, rings, starburst) rather than translation of a whole camera or a whole rigid object across the frame. The two exceptions — the S06 pan and the S12→S13 Moon flight — are the only translation-type motions in the video. | Per the reference-fidelity rule, no zoom, parallax, particle system, or camera shake should be added anywhere motion is not explicitly listed in `MOTION_EVENTS.csv`. |
| TRANSITION LANGUAGE | Hard cuts dominate (11 of 14 shot boundaries); a small number of shots share a continuous static background across a cut (S04→S09 reuse E03 exactly). No crossfades or wipes were observed at any shot boundary. | None observed. |
| ASSET REUSE PATTERN | Heavy reuse of the beam/glow motif (G03/G05) and the Earth/Moon iconography family across otherwise-different shots; the plasma-dome background (E03/G07/G08) is reused verbatim between S04 and S09 as a "callback" rather than redrawn. | Each reuse is noted per-asset in `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`'s OTHER_APPEARANCES column; do not create duplicate image prompts for these. |

## Evidence and measurement conventions
- Frame numbering: 30fps constant frame rate, frame 0 = first video frame, frame 3717 = last (3718 total frames, 123.933333s).
- All IN/OUT values in `TIMELINE.csv` / `MOTION_EVENTS.csv` are frame numbers; DURATION is given as `frames/seconds`.
- Shot boundaries were located via ffmpeg scene-change scoring (`select='gt(scene,0.10)'`) cross-checked against dense (±0.2-0.4s) native-frame-rate windows around every candidate; sub-shot state boundaries and long continuous motions (the S08 ring wrap, the S13 comet flight) were confirmed via 1s/4s interval sampling rather than every native frame, so their exact boundary frame is a best estimate (±1s) rather than frame-perfect.
- "Static hold" means no materially different frame content was found across the sampled frames within that state's range.


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# WAY 1 — CapCut Rebuild

Reference `02_analysis/TIMELINE.csv`, `02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`, `02_analysis/MOTION_EVENTS.csv`, `05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md` for canonical facts; this file gives only the CapCut build actions. Import `AU01` (the original audio track, or a re-recorded/licensed replacement — see NOTE below) onto A1 for the full project length before building any shot.

**NOTE on audio:** no transcript exists (see `05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md`). Every AUDIO SYNC line below cues off the five *measured* silence gaps and off "continuous mixed audio" generically — do not attempt to cut on specific words.

SOURCE STATES: F01.0 → F01.1 → F01.2

KEYFRAMES: V4 opacity 0→100 at 0:02.000 (A01); V4 width scale 100%→20% between 0:04.000 and 0:04.200 (A02, fastest defensible interpretation of a same-second reveal).

## Reuse decisions
- S09 reuses IMG04's fully-escalated end frame (after its own F04.3 animation) verbatim as a static image — it is the same cross-section composition already established in S04; regenerating it would duplicate an asset the reference itself reuses.
- S13 does not get its own IMG entry: because S12's flash-impact animation (A17) already transitions the Moon from grey (IMG11's starting state) to its post-impact appearance, S13's flight animation (A18) continues directly from that same generation's last frame rather than starting a fresh image.
- IMG06 is generated wider than 9:16 specifically so the S06 camera pan (A11) can be produced as a crop/position animation over one plate instead of two separate images.
- IMG09, IMG10, and IMG11 all reuse the same small grey Moon icon design; they are still three separate image prompts because each sits in a materially different composition (shaded-Earth establishing shot, simplified-schematic diagram, and wide beam-only shot respectively).

## R12 what_if_earths_water_suddenly_disappear

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA — what_if_earths_water_suddenly_disappear

Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file states only what recurs across the whole video.

## CHARACTER DNA
All human figures are minimal black-outline stick figures (circle head, single-line limbs, no facial features beyond occasional simple marks) — the recognizable "xkcd what if?" house style, consistent with the illustration family used elsewhere in this project. The host (C01) is the only character who recurs across non-adjacent shots (S01, S13, S15); every other character is scene-local.

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
Nine distinct backdrop environments (E01–E09), each confined to its own shot(s), reflecting a genuinely multi-scene explainer rather than a single locked set. All backgrounds are flat line-art with sparse color fill (white/gray/black, plus red used only for warning/danger/branding moments — title card, credits, heat gradient, engulfment rays).

## OBJECT DNA
Small watercraft (sailboat/kayak) and ship/fleet icon marks recur at multiple scales across the beach and depth-scale shots (O02, O05) — the same simple silhouette redrawn larger or smaller depending on the diagram's zoom level. Creature silhouettes (fish/whale/dolphin, O07) are the only object explicitly reused across non-adjacent shots (the S10 jar-diagram sequence and the S16/S17 aquarium epilogue), functioning as a visual callback.

## COLOR PALETTE
Overwhelmingly black-line-on-white/gray, matching this project's other xkcd-style sources. Red is reserved for exactly four purposes: the title card (S02), the runaway-heat gradient (S14), the sun-engulfment rays (S15), and the credits card (S18) — i.e., red consistently marks "branding" or "danger/heat" moments, never ordinary narrative content.

## LIGHTING
Flat, shadowless line-art throughout; no lighting model beyond solid-fill vs. outline. The only "lighting" event is the red gradient wash in S14/S15, which is a color/heat metaphor rather than a literal light source change.

## CAMERA / FRAMING
No physical camera; all "shots" are discrete diagram compositions cut against each other. Every shot uses a single locked framing internally (no pans, no handheld motion) — the only zoom-like event is the S09 zoom-out from the dual-panel depth comparison to the full Mariana Trench profile (A14), which is a diagram-scale transform, not a camera move. 17 of 18 shot boundaries are corroborated by measured `ffmpeg scdet` score spikes (see `00_source/SOURCE_MANIFEST.md`); the 18th is simply the video's natural end.

## COMPOSITION
Two recurring composition templates: (1) the "host" template — a stick figure beside a blackboard occupying the left third of frame, content drawn inside the blackboard on the right two-thirds (S01, S13, S15); (2) the "cross-section" template — a horizontal reference line (sea level or ground level) with a labeled vertical/depth scale, used for every water-level and geological diagram (S04–S09, S14).

## TYPOGRAPHY
Three recurring text systems (T01–T03, see `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`): a bold Q-card/question style, a bold aside/exclamation caption style (VACUUM, GASP!, WHEEZE!, WORSE? FOR WHO?, Hi!), and a small measurement/chemistry label style (depth numbers, timer values, chemical formulas). All appear to be a single consistent sans-serif family at different weights/sizes rather than distinct fonts.

## GRAPHICS
14 distinct overlay graphics (G01–G14), the largest graphic inventory in this project to date, reflecting the video's greater topical range (drainage physics, marine biology, atmospheric chemistry, geology, astronomy). The "measurement overlay system" (G04: timers, scale bars, depth axes, brackets) is the single most-reused graphic, spanning 6 shots (S05–S10).

## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
Pure 2D hand-drawn-style vector line art; no 3D, no photographic elements, no camera-realistic lighting or texture anywhere in the video.

## DEPTH
No true depth-of-field or parallax; apparent "depth" in the cross-section diagrams (S04–S09) is communicated entirely through a vertical depth-scale axis and relative object size, not through actual foreground/background blur or layering.

## MOTION LANGUAGE
Motion in this video is dominated by STATE_REPLACEMENT (content swaps: graphics appearing/clearing, fills changing) and SEQUENTIAL continuous changes (fire spreading, gradient intensifying, objects descending) — see `MOTION_EVENTS.csv`. Only two motion events are genuine physical translations of a character/object through space (A03 sailboat capsize, A20 figure+dog+boat departure); everything else is either a value/label change, a fill/color change, or a fade.

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
Nearly all 18 shot boundaries are hard CUTs. Two exceptions are evidenced by measured near-silence audio gaps and gray full-frame intermediate frames: the S06→S07 boundary (fades to solid gray before the deep-ocean panel appears, corroborated by a measured 58.7–58.9s audio near-silence gap) and the S07 shot's own opening (also preceded by the same fade). No wipes, slides, or other transition types were observed.

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
Lower overall reuse than `weird_and_worrying_questions` in absolute terms (most graphics/objects/environments are single-shot, reflecting the wide topical range) but higher character/text-system reuse for the recurring "host" device, which structurally bookends and punctuates the video (S01 intro question → S13 mid-video punchline → S15 closing epilogue). The measurement-overlay system (G04) and the underwater cross-section backdrop (E04) are the two most-reused non-character assets (6 and 6 shots respectively... actually E04 spans 4 shots, G04 spans 6 — see `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` for exact OTHER_APPEARANCES counts).


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# CapCut Rebuild — what_if_earths_water_suddenly_disappear

## 1. Project setup
- CANVAS / ASPECT RATIO: 16:9 landscape
- RESOLUTION: 1920x1080
- FPS: 24
- TOTAL DURATION: 183.792s (4411 frames)
- BACKGROUND: white (default for all diagram shots except S02/S18 red cards and S06–S09/S15 dark/space panels)
- MASTER AUDIO: AU01 (undifferentiated narration+music mix), placed on A1 for the full runtime
- GLOBAL FONT/TEXT SYSTEM: one bold sans-serif family at 3 weights — T01 (question-card), T02 (bold caption/exclamation), T03 (small measurement/chemistry label). Reference `../02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` for exact usage per shot.
- GLOBAL COLOR RULE: black line-art on white/gray by default; red reserved for the title card, credits card, the S14 heat gradient, and the S15 engulfment rays — never used elsewhere.
- GLOBAL EFFECTS: none beyond opacity fades at the S06/S07 gray-fade transition and the S10 seaplane→jar-diagram dissolve.

Characters: C01–C06 · Environments: E01–E09 · Objects: O01–O08 · Graphics: G01–G14 · Text systems: T01–T03 · Audio: AU01. Full descriptions in `../02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`.

## R13 what_if_the_moon_were_made_of_protons

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA — what_if_the_moon_were_made_of_protons

Global, evidence-supported production patterns. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file records only what repeats across shots. IDs reference `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` / `MOTION_EVENTS.csv`.

## CHARACTER DNA
- Repeated rule: a single plain white-outline stick figure (C01) — round bald head, no facial features beyond simple eyes/mouth marks, thin limb lines — represents the narrator/reactor throughout the diagram-heavy first two-thirds of the video (S01, S02, S04).
- Exceptions or limits: a second, visually distinct stick figure (C02, wavy/curly hair) appears once, only in S08, for a single joke aside. No other characters appear.

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
- Repeated rule: two background families alternate — (a) a flat white "whiteboard" canvas (E01) for scientific-diagram shots, and (b) a black background (E03 explosion / E05 starfield) for the more dramatic/cosmic beats. A third, one-off grey palette (E04) marks the single "real-world consequence" cutaway (S07).
- Exceptions or limits: E02 (ground/horizon line) appears only once, layered onto E01 for S04.

## OBJECT / GRAPHIC DNA
- Repeated rule: every concept is illustrated with a self-contained hand-drawn-style vector icon (circles, dashed orbit rings, arrows, funnels) labeled with small black text; icons are rarely reused verbatim but repeat a consistent "circle + label" visual grammar (G02/G03/G08/G11 all use a circle-plus-caption pattern; G05/G12/G16 all use an arrow-or-funnel-plus-label pattern).
- Exceptions or limits: G08 ("ELECTRON MOON") is the only icon drawn twice at different scales (full-size in S05, miniature in S06) — a deliberate callback rather than a new design.

## COLOR PALETTE
- Repeated rule: near-monochrome black/white/grey linework throughout, with a single reserved accent color — red — used exclusively for two purposes: (1) rejection/annotation marks (G04) and (2) all "aside" caption text (T01: "200,000 MOLES OF MOLES", "DARK ENERGY", "WHAT A BEAUTIFUL DAY", "HO HUM", "LA LA LA").
- Exceptions or limits: none observed; red never appears on any core diagram label (T03) or dialogue caption (T02).

## LIGHTING
- Not applicable in the photographic sense — all content is flat vector/sketch illustration. "Lighting" is simulated only via background value: bright/white diagram shots vs. a bright radial flash (S02) vs. solid black (S08/S09).

## CAMERA / FRAMING
- Repeated rule: every shot uses a static, locked camera — no pans, zooms, or parallax were observed anywhere in the video. All apparent scale change is achieved by redrawing/regenerating graphic elements at a new size (e.g., the growing cloud in S04, the growing circle in S09), never by moving a virtual camera.
- Exceptions or limits: none. This holds for all 9 shots without exception.

## COMPOSITION
- Repeated rule: diagram shots are typically composed with the primary graphic in the upper-to-middle portion of the tall 9:16 frame and any caption/character content below it, leaving generous white/black negative space around the edges.
- Exceptions or limits: S07's collapse illustration and S09's growing circle both intentionally break this by using more of the full frame as the shot progresses.

## TYPOGRAPHY
- Repeated rule: three consistent text roles are held throughout — red hand-drawn-style captions (T01) for narrator asides/jokes, black plain captions (T02) for character dialogue, and small black label text (T03) integrated directly into each diagram. No other font families or colors are used for text anywhere in the video.
- Exceptions or limits: none.

## GRAPHICS
- Repeated rule: every major concept gets one dedicated icon (see Object/Graphic DNA); icons are additive within a shot (new elements appear alongside old ones) rather than being redrawn from scratch, except at hard shot cuts.
- Exceptions or limits: none beyond the G08 reuse noted above.

## ILLUSTRATION / STYLE
- Repeated rule: loose, hand-drawn/sketch vector illustration style throughout (visible line waver, no photographic or 3D-rendered elements) — consistent with a "science explainer" whiteboard-doodle aesthetic.
- Exceptions or limits: none.

## DEPTH
- Repeated rule: all content is flat 2D with no simulated depth-of-field, parallax, or perspective camera; the "stretched fabric" graphic (G10) and "funnel" graphic (G12) simulate depth *within* a flat illustration (a drawn 3D-looking well), not via any camera or layering technique.

## MOTION LANGUAGE
- Repeated rule: motion is almost always either (a) a graphic element being drawn on/revealed (text pop-ins, rejection scribbles, new icons appearing) or (b) a single icon growing/expanding/radiating in place (field lines, cloud growth, starburst, circle growth). No independent camera motion, parallax, or multi-object choreography was observed anywhere.
- Exceptions or limits: A02 (S02) is the only shot with any character-body motion (a small recoil/crouch), and even that is a minor, brief gesture rather than sustained movement.

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
- Repeated rule: every shot boundary in this video is a hard CUT; no dissolves, wipes, or other transition effects were observed or detected by the scene-cut filter at either threshold.
- Exceptions or limits: none — all 8 shot boundaries are confirmed hard cuts (see `TIMELINE.csv` TRANSITION_IN/OUT columns).

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
- Repeated rule: most graphics (G01–G07, G09–G15) are single-use, purpose-built for one shot's specific beat; only the character (C01), the three text systems (T01–T03), the "ELECTRON MOON" icon (G08), and the background families (E01, E05) recur across multiple shots.
- Exceptions or limits: this is a lower-reuse video than a typical talking-head or recurring-set explainer — nearly every shot introduces at least one new bespoke diagram, reflecting its fast-moving, joke-a-beat comedic-explainer structure.

## Evidence and measurement conventions
- All 8 shot boundaries are OBSERVED via `ffmpeg` scene-cut detection (5 at threshold 0.25, 3 additional at threshold 0.10); see `00_source/SOURCE_MANIFEST.md`.
- All internal visual-state boundaries and all motion timings were derived from 1-second-interval frame sampling (not exhaustive per-frame verification) and are labeled LIKELY in `TIMELINE.csv` / `MOTION_EVENTS.csv` accordingly.
- No camera movement, easing curve, exact font, exact music/SFX, or original authoring tool is claimed anywhere in this analysis.

## Master continuity references
- **C01 (narrator character):** minimalist black-outline stick figure — a single perfect circle for a head with two small dot eyes and a simple curved-line mouth, no hair, thin single-stroke arms and legs, no fill color, hand-drawn/slightly wavering line quality.
- **C02 (aside character):** identical stick-figure body language and line style to C01, but with a scribbly/wavy short-hair outline on top of the head as the one distinguishing feature.
- **Global style:** loose hand-drawn ink/vector line-art illustration, flat 2D, no photographic or 3D-rendered elements, no camera perspective/depth-of-field; black strokes on either a plain white or plain black background, with red reserved exclusively for annotation/rejection marks and aside captions.

## Reuse decisions
This video's fast, joke-per-beat structure produces almost no visual repetition between shots (see `../02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md`, Asset Reuse Pattern), so no image is reused verbatim across shots. Two internal first/last-frame pairs are used instead of extra intermediate images, maximizing reuse *within* a shot: IMG09→IMG10 (S06's zoom-to-black-hole payoff) and IMG14→IMG15 (S09's closing circle-growth payoff). IMG03→IMG04 and IMG05→IMG06 are similar within-shot pairs used where the composition changes too much for one image to cover the whole shot via animation alone.

## R14 what_would_a_magnitude_15_earthquake_be

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA — what_would_a_magnitude_15_earthquake_be

Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; do not repeat it here.

## CHARACTER DNA
Stick figures throughout: plain circle head (no facial features except in a couple of speech-bubble reaction beats), thin single-stroke limbs, no color fill. Identical drawing convention to the host character in every other video already reconstructed in this project. Secondary animals (cat, dog, mouse) use the same simple single-stroke line-art convention, no shading. — OBSERVED

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
Backgrounds are almost always a flat off-white/light-gray canvas with no horizon or setting except where the gag specifically requires one (the newspaper's cornfield inset, the outdoor tree scenes). No parallax layers, no depth-of-field. — OBSERVED

## OBJECT DNA
All illustrated objects (globe, sun, seismograph, truck, furniture) are simple black-outline line art on the same flat canvas, redrawn/modified in place rather than replaced with a differently-styled asset when their state changes (e.g. the globe gains cracks and a debris ring but keeps the same base silhouette). — OBSERVED

## COLOR PALETTE
Overwhelmingly black-line-on-off-white, matching the rest of the project's "xkcd what if" videos. Two deliberate color accents: red, used exclusively for (a) the "xkcd's what if?" bumper/credits card background and (b) hand-scribbled emphasis marks (Richter Scale strikethrough, ruler tick marks, quake epicenter rings). No other color appears. — OBSERVED

## LIGHTING
Flat, shadowless line-art throughout; no rendered lighting model. — OBSERVED

## CAMERA / FRAMING
Every shot is a locked, static 2D camera — no pans, zooms, or parallax were measured anywhere in the video. All apparent "movement" is the illustrated subject changing (label swaps, object animation, particle motion), not camera motion. — OBSERVED

## COMPOSITION
Consistent single-focal-point compositions: one dominant illustration per state, usually paired with a large "MAGNITUDE ##" headline directly above it, and a persistent vertical reference ruler at frame-left for most of the ascending/descending sequence (S05–S12). — OBSERVED

## TYPOGRAPHY
Two font treatments: (1) a bold, slightly hand-drawn-style sans-serif for the "MAGNITUDE ##" headlines and most captions; (2) a looser, more hand-lettered style for onomatopoeia/sound-effect text (WHUMP, CRASH, PLINK, CLICK, KERTHUMP). Intro question text and LIVE-TV captions sit in light-gray rounded rectangles / black-bordered boxes respectively. — OBSERVED

## GRAPHICS
Recurring motifs: the vertical "Moment Magnitude" ruler (present from S05 through S12, growing then implicitly continuing off-frame during the descending scale), red hand-scribble emphasis marks, cloud-shaped thought bubbles, small radiating shake-line clusters for impacts, and a reusable explosion-burst graphic (appears 3 times: NYC example, Earth breakup, sun/Magnitude 25). — OBSERVED

## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
Pure 2D hand-drawn vector/line-art style; no 3D rendering anywhere, including the "3500 km" tectonic block diagram, which is drawn in a flat isometric-style illustration rather than true 3D. — OBSERVED

## DEPTH
No true depth layering; foreground/background separation is implied only by relative scale and left/right placement, not by parallax or blur. — OBSERVED

## MOTION LANGUAGE
Two motion categories only were measured: (1) instantaneous full-composition swaps between magnitude values (the dominant pattern — see `MOTION_EVENTS.csv` RELATIONSHIP=STATE_REPLACEMENT rows), and (2) genuine continuous motion reserved for specific illustrated physics — falling objects (leaf, feather, cat), particle flow (hourglass sand, debris cascade), and explosive/fracturing expansion (Earth breakup, sun burst, magnetar field-line pulse). No decorative camera motion, parallax, glow, or idle-loop animation was found anywhere; none should be added in reconstruction. — OBSERVED

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
All 16 shots are joined by hard cuts (`ffmpeg scdet` score ≥5.4 at every shot boundary) except the final shot change into the ending vignette, which uses a brief (~1s) full black-screen wipe (S14→S15 via S15/F15.0). No cross-fades or dissolves were measured. — OBSERVED

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
Heavy reuse of a small set of recurring assets across otherwise distinct states: the host stick figure (C01), the vertical ruler (O05), the globe (E03, reused with escalating damage states), the sun (O07, reused with escalating states), the explosion-burst graphic (G03), and the debris/fragment graphic (G04). The "MAGNITUDE ##" text system (T01) is the single most-repeated element in the entire video, appearing in nearly every state. See `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` OTHER_APPEARANCES column for the full reuse map. — OBSERVED


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# CapCut Rebuild — what_would_a_magnitude_15_earthquake_be

FPS: 24

GLOBAL FONT/TEXT SYSTEM: Bold rounded sans-serif for "MAGNITUDE ##" headlines and most captions (T01/T03); looser hand-lettered comic font for onomatopoeia (T02)
GLOBAL COLOR RULE: Black line art on off-white by default; red reserved for the bumper/credits background and hand-scribble emphasis marks (strike-through, tick marks, epicenter rings)
GLOBAL EFFECTS IF ANY: None — no filters, LUTs, vignettes, or camera-shake effects were measured anywhere in the source

MEDIA TO IMPORT: See `../02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` for the full list (C01-C05 characters, E01-E06 environments, O01-O17 objects, G01-G07 graphics, T01-T03 text systems, AU01 audio). Reference IDs below rather than re-describing each asset.
