## R15 worlds-largest-cities-what-if

### 02_analysis/VISUAL_DNA.md
# Visual DNA (global rules — see TIMELINE.csv for per-state detail)

## CHARACTER DNA
- One recurring stick-figure narrator (C01): circle head, no facial features, single-line limbs, holds a paper/clipboard. Appears only in S01 (0–4.42s), static pose throughout.
- Two decorative sticker vignettes (G04, G05) contain their own tiny line-art figures (mountain/landscape scene; two seated characters), each used exactly once, unrelated in style to C01 (simpler/rounder, no shared model).

## ENVIRONMENT DNA
- S01: a hand-drawn classroom blackboard on an off-white page background.
- S02: one continuous oversized hand-drawn world map (E01) — the entire back 79 seconds of the video is a camera move across this single asset, not a sequence of separate map graphics.

## OBJECT DNA
- Globes (O01/O02) are line-art, gray/white, appear only in S01.
- City markers (G02) are a single reused dot+label template applied 20 times.

## COLOR PALETTE (E01, the map)
- Teal — open ocean.
- Cyan — inland/flooded water or a shallow-sea band.
- Gray — exposed seabed / bare rock.
- Yellow (pale) — arid/desert climate band.
- Green — vegetated/temperate band.
- Magenta/purple — city marker dots (G02), the only saturated accent color against the muted map palette.
- Red — the one hand-drawn annotation circle (G03), the only other saturated accent color, used once for emphasis.
S01 (board scene) is grayscale/off-white only — no color appears until the cut into S02.

## LIGHTING
Flat, uniform, no shading/gradient beyond the hand-inked line work and flat color fills. No day/night or light-direction cues.

## CAMERA / FRAMING
- S01: locked-off, no camera movement.
- S02: a single moving crop window over one large map image. Movement alternates between FAST blurred pan/push bursts (the norm — 8 of 9 transitions) and one slow unblurred pan (A08, ~48–55s). No rotation, no parallax, no depth-of-field change anywhere in the video.

## COMPOSITION
9:16 vertical throughout. S01 stacks title card (top) / illustration (mid) / character (bottom). S02 has no persistent UI chrome — the map fills the frame edge-to-edge; city labels sit directly on the map near their dot.

## TYPOGRAPHY
- Title card (T01): black serif, two centered lines, on a rounded gray card — S01 only.
- Map labels (continent names, city names): hand-lettered look (uneven baseline, marker-style strokes), black, no card/background — S02 only, baked into or overlaid on the map.

## GRAPHICS / ILLUSTRATION STYLE
Uniform "hand-drawn doodle/whiteboard" style across both shots and both sticker vignettes: black ink outlines, minimal or flat color fill, no gradients, no 3D shading, no photographic elements anywhere in the video.

## MOTION LANGUAGE
Two motion types only, observed nowhere else:
1. STATE_REPLACEMENT (object pop-in/swap) — used for O01→O02 and every G02/G03/G04/G05 appearance.
2. PAN/PUSH with motion blur on the fast bursts, unblurred on the one slow pan (A08) — used only for the S02 camera moves.
No zoom-breathing, no parallax, no character motion (C01 is static throughout its whole appearance), no particle/glow effects anywhere.

## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
- S01 internal (F01.0→F01.1): straight content swap on the same locked composition, no visible wipe/fade.
- S01→S02: the only hard, blurred "whip" transition in the video, corroborated by a ~0.35s audio near-silence dip at the cut point.
- All S02 internal "cuts" (the scene-detector hits at 8.83/18.0/25.58/35.42/41.92/65.29/72.38s) are NOT shot changes — they are fast-pan motion-blur bursts across the same continuous map asset E01. Treat them as camera moves, not edits.

## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
E01 (the map) is the backbone: generated/drawn once, reused for the entire second half via camera movement only. G02 (city pin+label) is a single template reused 20 times. Everything else (T01, C01, O01, O02, G03, G04, G05) is single-shot/single-use.


### 03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md
# CapCut Rebuild

Reference `02_analysis/TIMELINE.csv`, `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`, `MOTION_EVENTS.csv` for IDs. Descriptions are not repeated here.

## Project setup
- CANVAS / ASPECT RATIO: 9:16
- RESOLUTION: 1080x1920
- FPS: 24
- TOTAL DURATION: 00:00.000–01:23.333
- BACKGROUND: off-white (S01) → fully covered by E01 (S02), no letterboxing
- MASTER AUDIO: AU01, one continuous clip, full length, placed on A1
- GLOBAL FONT/TEXT SYSTEM: T01 = a bold/rounded serif for the title card; G02 city labels = a casual hand-lettered font (CapCut's "Marker"/"Handwriting" preset family is the closest built-in match — POSSIBLE, not confirmed)
- GLOBAL COLOR RULE: grayscale board scene (S01) vs. full climate-palette map (S02) — no color grade/LUT beyond the source asset colors
- GLOBAL EFFECTS: none (no filters, no vignette, no grain observed)

## Media to import
- T01 — title card (text box + rounded-rect background shape, built natively in CapCut, no import needed)
- C01 — stick-figure narrator PNG
- O01 — single globe PNG
- O02 — two-globes-plus-arrow PNG (or two separate globe PNGs + CapCut arrow shape)
- E01 — master map JPG/PNG (must be wide enough that the S02 crop window never runs out of image — see FIDELITY LIMITATION below)
- G02 — one city-pin dot PNG (reused), 20x native CapCut text labels
- G03 — red circle annotation PNG (or drawn live with CapCut's shape/brush tool)
- G04 — landscape vignette sticker PNG
- G05 — dialogue vignette sticker PNG
- AU01 — full-length audio/music+VO track

## Shot build

### S01 — 00:00.000–00:04.420
SOURCE STATES: F01.0 → F01.1
MEDIA: T01, C01, O01, O02
TRACK STACK:
- V3 — T01 (title card)

BUILD:
1. Add AU01 to A1, full length.
2. Add T01 text box, position top-third, duration 0:00–0:04.42 (holds unchanged the whole shot).
3. Add C01 PNG to V1, same duration, static, no keyframes (APPROVED: no motion observed).
4. Add O01 to V2, 0:00–~0:02.00 (APPROXIMATE cut point — verify against your own copy of the source before locking).
5. Cut V2 to O02 at ~0:02.00, hold to 0:04.42.
KEYFRAMES: none — every element in S01 is a static hold (confirms MOTION_EVENTS A01 as a straight replace, not a tween).
TOOLS: text tool (rounded background), cutout/PNG overlay, cut (no transition effect — it's a straight replace within the same locked shot).

TRANSITION: hard cut out at 4.42s into S02.

END STATE: F01.1.

### S02 — 00:04.420–00:83.333 (single continuous "shot", built as ONE crop-and-pan move over E01)

2. Turn on position/scale keyframes on E01. Because CapCut keyframes are the only real path to a "pan across a giant image" in this tool, treat each MOTION_EVENTS PAN row (A03–A10) as one pair of keyframes (start-of-burst / end-of-burst), holding position flat between bursts (the HOLD states in TIMELINE.csv):
KEYFRAMES (position values are APPROXIMATE — set by eye against your own copy of E01, using each state's literal description as the target framing; do not treat these as measured pixel coordinates):

4. 5. Add each G02 dot+label pair on V3 at its own appearance point per TIMELINE.csv / MOTION_EVENTS.csv (R01/R02/R05), then let it hold (opacity 100%, no further keyframes) through the rest of the video once added.

7. Add G04 on V4, ~0:44.50–~0:55.00 (its own clip, parented/keyframed to track the same position deltas as E01's pan during that window, since it is map-anchored — see FIDELITY LIMITATION).
8. Add G05 on V4, ~0:76.00–0:83.333.
TOOLS: keyframes, position, scale, crop, mask (if you need to hard-crop E01's edges), opacity (for G02 pop-ins), blur/speed-ramp transition.
TEXT: 20x G02 city names — exact spellings and order of first appearance: Mexico City, Jakarta, Kolkata, Delhi, Hong Kong, Mumbai, Karachi, Manila, Shanghai, Seoul, Osaka, Tokyo, Beijing, Moscow, Cairo, London, New York City, Los Angeles, São Paulo, Buenos Aires.
TRANSITION IN: whip-zoom blur from S01 (A02).
TRANSITION OUT: none — video ends on the F02.8 hold.
AUDIO SYNC: AU01 continues unbroken from S01; no further confirmed sync points beyond the one silence dip already placed at the S01/S02 boundary.
END STATE: F02.8 (final frame of the file).

FIDELITY LIMITATION: CapCut cannot natively "walk a virtual camera along a fixed-position sticker" — G04/G05 tracking the map pan (CAMERA_SUBJECT_COUPLED, motion A08) must be hand-keyframed to move in lockstep with E01's own keyframes rather than being a single automatic parent/child relationship (CapCut has no true parenting). Closest method: keyframe G04/G05's position with the same deltas you used for E01 in that time window.


### 04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md
# Image Prompts

Reference `02_analysis/ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` / `TIMELINE.csv` for IDs. Only 3 unique source images are required for this entire video — everything else is either a static text/shape overlay (built in final assembly, not generated) or a reused crop of IMG02.

## IMG01
- USED BY SHOTS/STATES: S01 (F01.0, F01.1)
- SOURCE STATE: opening frame
- REUSE RELATIONSHIP: single use — this is the one board illustration; F01.0→F01.1 is a same-image local edit (swap the globe content), not a new image. If your generator can't edit in place, generate IMG01 twice (IMG01a = single globe, IMG01b = two globes+arrow) with identical style/composition instructions below, changing only the "OBJECTS" line.

### 04_image_to_video/ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md
# Animation Prompts

## Compliance note (read first)
Every observed motion in this video is either (a) a camera crop moving across a static painted image (E01/IMG02), or (b) a static overlay/text popping on and holding. There is no observed independent motion of any drawn element — no character movement, no water/cloud animation, no object travel. Per rule 28 (static scenes) and rule 22 (I2V motion should be reserved for real change-through-time), generating genuine I2V clips for the map pans would manufacture motion detail (drift risk) the source never asked for. **ANIMATION REQUIRED: NO for every S02 camera move — reconstruct them as crop/position keyframes on the still IMG02 master plate during final assembly (identical technique to the CapCut build's E01 keyframes), not as generative I2V passes.** This is the correct lazy-and-faithful call, not a shortcut around a real requirement.

The only place a generative I2V pass is defensible is the single whip-zoom-blur cut into the map (A02), and even that is optional — a plain blur-transition effect in the assembly tool achieves the same observed result with zero drift risk.

## A02 (optional — transition effect, not required)
- SHOT ID: S01→S02
- SOURCE IMAGE: IMG01b (two-globe board state)
- SOURCE STATE: F01.1
- TARGET STATE: F02.0
- CLIP DURATION: ~0.6s
- MOVING ELEMENT: camera only (whole-frame push)
- STATIC ANCHORS: none (full-frame transition)
- ANIMATION PROMPT (≤500 chars): "Fast camera push forward into the scene with heavy directional motion blur, as if rushing toward the blackboard. Hold for the first 0.1s, then blur and accelerate for 0.4s, ending fully blurred. No new objects appear. Keep the illustration style and line weight identical throughout."
- FIDELITY RISK: If your I2V tool invents new geometry mid-blur (common drift), skip this and use a plain editor blur/zoom transition instead — it's the safer, equally faithful option.

## All S02 camera moves (A03–A10): NO ANIMATION PROMPT NEEDED
Build these as crop/position/scale keyframes on the static IMG02 plate in final assembly:
| ID | Behavior | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| A03 | fast blurred pan | ~0.5s | add a brief motion-blur/speed-ramp effect over the crop-move to sell the "fast burst" look |
| A04 | fast blurred pan | ~0.5s | same |
| A05 | fast blurred pan | ~0.5s | same |
| A06 | fast blurred pan | ~0.5s | same |
| A07 | fast blurred push-in | ~0.5s | same, tighter scale target |
| A08 | slow unblurred pan | ~17s | the one exception — animate as a smooth linear/eased crop move, no blur effect |
| A09 | fast blurred pan | ~0.5s | same as A03–A07 |
| A10 | fast blurred pan | ~0.5s | same |

## Reveals (R01, R02, R04, R05, R06): NO ANIMATION PROMPT NEEDED
G02 city pins, G03 red circle, G04 and G05 stickers are all static pop-ins/holds — add as overlay images/text with a simple opacity fade (or hard cut-in, per OBSERVED — the exact fade-vs-cut style could not be isolated at 1fps sampling) in final assembly. Generating these via I2V would be pure drift risk for zero benefit.
